decisions.reason: As a low-noise variant that extends the established infrared-heating business, it is likely kept while management tolerates some uncertainty because the product fits existing capabilities and service channels.

Its dedicated product page suggests initial strategic attention, and absent clear signs of serious underperformance it would likely stay as an incremental offering close to the firm's aspiration level.
This radiant-heater variant appears more exposed to overlap and niche demand, so if results fell short of aspirations management would reallocate resources to stronger core lines and new development.
Because it is a broader product line with several models in a core technology area, the firm has more reason and more organisational slack to continue and refine it rather than withdraw it quickly.

A standard plaque-heater offer supports the core portfolio and likely helps cover mainstream customer needs, so management would tend to retain it unless performance clearly lagged comparable products.
Given its apparent overlap with the broader tube-heater line, this product is the strongest candidate for problemistic search and pruning if it has not delivered distinct enough results.
